questions.q: What does the summary say keeps people stuck in unhappy situations?
a: Assumptions and fear of the unknown
A lack of ambition and talent
Too many advisers and opinions
Bad luck and unfair circumstances
questions.why: Lesson 1 says we convince ourselves we know what will happen and stay in a comfort zone of assumptions.

questions.q: What is overgeneralizing, as described in the summary?
a: Drawing a broad conclusion from very little evidence
Considering every outcome before deciding
Asking experts to check your facts
Adapting quickly to unfamiliar situations
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines overgeneralizing as deciding from very little evidence and applying it to a larger context.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest you avoid overgeneralizing?
a: Zoom out from single events and average out the facts
Rely on your first instinct in the moment
Ask only people who already agree with you
Avoid making any decision at all
questions.why: Lesson 2 advises zooming out from single events and averaging facts instead of judging from one case.

questions.q: Which step does the summary recommend before making a decision?
a: Fact-check your data and seek a second opinion
Decide quickly to avoid overthinking
Trust your emotions over the numbers
Keep the plan private from your team
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends basing decisions on facts and asking others for a second opinion.

questions.q: How does the summary describe the value of people in decision-making?
a: The right people can be your most valuable asset
People usually add bias to a decision
Advisers are only useful to CEOs
A team slows down every process
questions.why: Lesson 3 calls the right people possibly the most valuable asset you have when deciding.
